## Summary of Changes Hello @chrislusf, I'm Gemini Code Assist[^1]! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed! This pull request significantly enhances the robustness of SQL-backed filer operations, particularly for MySQL/MariaDB, by implementing a retry mechanism for transient database errors. This change aims to prevent `Input/output error` issues, especially during high-concurrency operations like `chown` on large file sets, by automatically retrying operations that encounter deadlocks or lock wait timeouts. The solution introduces a flexible callback system for error identification and integrates it into the fundamental data manipulation methods. ### Highlights * **Retryable Error Callback**: Introduced a `RetryableErrorCallback` function type to `AbstractSqlStore` to allow specific database implementations to define which errors are transient and should trigger a retry. * **SQL Operation Retries**: Wrapped the core `InsertEntry`, `UpdateEntry`, `DeleteEntry`, and `DeleteFolderChildren` SQL operations within the `AbstractSqlStore` with a `util.RetryUntil` mechanism, enabling automatic retries for transient errors. * **MySQL/MariaDB Specific Retries**: Configured the `MysqlStore` to utilize the new retry mechanism, specifically identifying MySQL errors 1213 (ER_LOCK_DEADLOCK) and 1205 (ER_LOCK_WAIT_TIMEOUT) as retryable conditions. * **Enhanced Retry Utility**: Modified the `util.RetryUntil` function to propagate the final error encountered if the operation ultimately fails or a non-retryable error occurs, providing clearer error handling. * **Unit Test Coverage**: Added comprehensive unit tests for the `util.RetryUntil` function to ensure its correct behavior under various success and failure scenarios. 🧠 **New Feature in Public Preview:** You can now enable **Memory** to help **Gemini Code Assist** learn from your team's feedback. This makes future code reviews more consistent and personalized to your project's style. **Click [here](https://codeassist.google/code-review/login) to enable Memory in your admin console.**
Using Gemini Code Assist
The full guide for Gemini Code Assist can be found on our [documentation page](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-github-code), here are some quick tips. Invoking Gemini You can request assistance from Gemini at any point by creating a comment using either `/gemini ` or `@gemini-code-assist `. Below is a summary of the supported commands on the current page. Feature | Command | Description --- | --- | --- Code Review | `/gemini review` | Performs a code review for the current pull request in its current state. Pull Request Summary | `/gemini summary` | Provides a summary of the current pull request in its current state. Comment | @gemini-code-assist | Responds in comments when explicitly tagged, both in pull request comments and review comments. Help | `/gemini help` | Displays a list of available commands. Customization To customize Gemini Code Assist for GitHub experience, repository maintainers can create a configuration file and/or provide a custom code review style guide (such as PEP-8 for Python) by creating and adding files to a `.gemini/` folder in the base of the repository. Detailed instructions can be found [here](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/customize-gemini-behavior-github). Limitations & Feedback Gemini Code Assist may make mistakes. Please leave feedback on any instances where its feedback is incorrect or counter productive. You can react with :thumbsup: and :thumbsdown: on @gemini-code-assist comments. If you're interested in giving your feedback about your experience with Gemini Code Assist for Github and other Google products, sign up [here](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_2cyuGuTWsEw84yG). You can also get AI-powered code generation, chat, as well as code reviews directly in the IDE at no cost with the [Gemini Code Assist IDE Extension](https://cloud.google.com/products/gemini/code-assist).
[^1]: Review the [Privacy Notices](https://policies.google.com/privacy), [Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy](https://policies.google.com/terms/generative-ai/use-policy), [Terms of Service](https://policies.google.com/terms), and learn how to configure Gemini Code Assist in GitHub [here](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/customize-gemini-behavior-github). Gemini can make mistakes, so double check it and [use code with caution](https://support.google.com/legal/answer/13505487).

📝 Walkthrough ## Walkthrough Adds configurable retry support for SQL write operations: `util.RetryUntil` now returns an error; `AbstractSqlStore` gets a `RetryableErrorCallback` and wraps insert/update/delete operations to optionally run via `RetryUntil`; MySQL store sets the callback for deadlock and lock-wait timeouts. ## Changes | Cohort / File(s) | Summary | |---|---| | **Retry Utility**
`weed/util/retry.go` | Changed `RetryUntil` signature to return `error`. On success returns `nil`; when `onErrFn` returns false, returns the error instead of breaking the loop. | | **Retry Tests**
`weed/util/retry_test.go` | New unit tests: `SucceedsImmediately`, `SucceedsAfterRetry`, `FailsNonRetryable` validating retry behavior and attempt counts. | | **Abstract SQL Store**
`weed/filer/abstract_sql/abstract_sql_store.go` | Added public field `RetryableErrorCallback func(err error) bool`. Refactored `InsertEntry`, `UpdateEntry`, `DeleteEntry`, `DeleteFolderChildren` into local `do*` closures and conditionally execute them via `util.RetryUntil` when callback is provided; preserved existing error handling, rows-affected checks, and bucket/table lifecycle logic. | | **MySQL Store**
`weed/filer/mysql/mysql_store.go` | Configured `RetryableErrorCallback` on `MysqlStore` to mark MySQL deadlock (`ER_LOCK_DEADLOCK`, 1213) and lock-wait timeout (`ER_LOCK_WAIT_TIMEOUT`, 1205) errors as retryable. | ## Sequence Diagram(s) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant App as Application participant Store as AbstractSqlStore participant Retry as util.RetryUntil participant Callback as RetryableErrorCallback participant DB as Database App->>Store: InsertEntry(...) alt RetryableErrorCallback is set Store->>Retry: RetryUntil(job) loop attempts Retry->>Store: invoke doInsert() Store->>DB: execute SQL DB-->>Store: success / error alt success Store-->>Retry: nil Retry-->>Store: return nil else error Store-->>Retry: error Retry->>Callback: RetryableErrorCallback(err) alt callback returns true Callback-->>Retry: true Retry->>Retry: wait & retry else callback returns false Callback-->>Retry: false Retry-->>Store: return error end end end else No callback Store->>DB: execute SQL directly DB-->>Store: success / error end Store-->>App: return result ``` ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 4 (Complex) | ⏱️ ~50 minutes ## Poem > 🐰 I nibble logs and count each try, > Deadlocks shiver as I hop by, > A retry here, a timeout spared, > My whiskers twitch — the rows repaired. ✨

The required threshold is 80.00%. | Write docstrings for the functions missing them to satisfy the coverage threshold. |

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues
